ct angiography.title: Acute Aortic Dissection
ct angiography.subtitle: Initial Medical Management
ct angiography.def: A contrast-enhanced CT scan that outlines the inside of the vessel lumen — fast enough and detailed enough to be the first-line test for suspected dissection.

ct angiography.title: Anticoagulant Reversal
ct angiography.subtitle: In Gastrointestinal Haemorrhage
ct angiography.def: Contrast-enhanced CT imaging of the vasculature, used here to localise an ongoing lower GI bleeding source before an endoscopic or interventional-radiology procedure is chosen.

aki.title: Acute Aortic Dissection
aki.subtitle: Initial Medical Management
aki.def: A sudden drop in kidney function. Here, a reason to individualise rather than enforce the SBP <120 target by default, since the kidney may already be under-perfused.

aki.title: Dexketoprofen vs Ibuprofen
aki.subtitle: Selecting an NSAID for Acute Pain
aki.def: A sudden drop in kidney function. NSAIDs remove a compensatory renal-prostaglandin mechanism, so AKI (or a low eGFR, or hypovolaemia) is a reason to avoid them rather than merely dose-reduce.

rass.title: Butyrophenone Selection
rass.subtitle: Acute Agitation & Hyperactive Delirium
rass.def: A 10-point scale (−5, unarousable, to +4, combative) used to document and trend a patient's level of agitation or sedation at the bedside. Validated in adult ICU patients; used here to make "reassess every 10–15 min" an objective, reproducible check rather than a subjective impression.

rass.title: Ketamine in Emergency and Critical Care
rass.subtitle: Indication-Based Decision Algorithm
rass.def: A validated scale used to grade a patient's level of sedation or agitation; used as the outcome measure in trials comparing ketamine with haloperidol for acute agitation.

ppi.title: Dexketoprofen vs Ibuprofen
ppi.subtitle: Selecting an NSAID for Acute Pain
ppi.def: An acid-suppressing drug added alongside an NSAID in patients with GI risk factors (prior ulcer, anticoagulant/antiplatelet use, age) to reduce the chance of NSAID-associated ulceration.

ppi.title: Anticoagulant Reversal
ppi.subtitle: In Gastrointestinal Haemorrhage
ppi.def: An acid-suppressing drug given at high dose after endoscopic haemostasis for upper GI bleeding, to create a less acidic environment that stabilises clot formation over the treated lesion.

mcid.title: Dexketoprofen vs Ibuprofen
mcid.subtitle: Selecting an NSAID for Acute Pain
mcid.def: The smallest change in a pain score a patient would perceive as meaningful. This page anchors it to roughly 10 mm on a 100 mm visual analogue scale — a slightly conservative rounding of Kelly's empirically measured ≈12 mm minimum clinically significant difference.

mcid.title: Lidocaine vs Prilocaine
mcid.subtitle: Local Anaesthesia for Laceration Repair
mcid.def: The smallest change in an outcome (here, roughly 1.3 points on a 0–10 pain scale, or a standardized effect size of about 0.5) that a patient would consider meaningful — used to judge whether a statistically real difference actually matters clinically.

mcid.title: Midazolam versus Clonazepam
mcid.subtitle: Seizures, Acute Agitation & Anxiety
mcid.def: The smallest size of effect, expressed here as Cohen's d, that this review treated as clinically meaningful rather than merely statistically detectable: below 0.2 is below the threshold, 0.2–0.49 small, 0.5–0.79 moderate, and 0.8 or more large.

mcid.title: Tenecteplase versus Alteplase
mcid.subtitle: Fibrinolysis in STEMI When Timely Primary PCI Is Not Available
mcid.def: The smallest difference that patients and clinicians would consider meaningful. This review prespecified an absolute standardised effect size (Cohen's d) of 0.20 as the MCID threshold for judging whether a statistically significant finding was also clinically important.

ufh.title: Anticoagulant Reversal
ufh.subtitle: In Gastrointestinal Haemorrhage
ufh.def: An injectable anticoagulant that potentiates antithrombin's inhibition of both thrombin and factor Xa. Fully neutralised by protamine sulfate, unlike LMWH.

ufh.title: Tenecteplase versus Alteplase
ufh.subtitle: Fibrinolysis in STEMI When Timely Primary PCI Is Not Available
ufh.def: An adjunctive anticoagulant option alongside fibrinolysis, used either instead of or historically before age- and renal-adjusted enoxaparin.

rsi.title: The Adult with Obesity
rsi.subtitle: In Emergency and Critical Care
rsi.def: A fast-onset induction and paralysis technique used when aspiration risk is high. The review specifically warns against under-dosing rocuronium for RSI by using a fixed adult dose.

rsi.title: Ketamine in Emergency and Critical Care
rsi.subtitle: Indication-Based Decision Algorithm
rsi.def: Near-simultaneous administration of an induction agent and a paralytic to secure the airway quickly, minimising aspiration risk; ketamine's role as an RSI induction agent is substantially revised by the 2025 RSI Trial covered in this tool.

esketamine.title: Ketamine in Head Injury
esketamine.subtitle: Safety Analysis & Complication Management
esketamine.def: The S(+)-enantiomer of ketamine, roughly twice as potent as the racemic mixture used elsewhere in this algorithm — doses are halved whenever esketamine is substituted — and associated with somewhat fewer cognitive disturbances on emergence.

esketamine.title: Ketamine in Emergency and Critical Care
esketamine.subtitle: Indication-Based Decision Algorithm
esketamine.def: The more potent enantiomer of racemic ketamine, with roughly three-fold greater NMDA receptor affinity; licensed in several countries for treatment-resistant depression.

grade.title: Midazolam versus Clonazepam
grade.subtitle: Seizures, Acute Agitation & Anxiety
grade.def: A structured system for rating how much confidence to place in a body of evidence for a specific outcome — from high down to very low — based on risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias.

grade.title: Tenecteplase versus Alteplase
grade.subtitle: Fibrinolysis in STEMI When Timely Primary PCI Is Not Available
grade.full: Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation
grade.def: The framework this review used to rate certainty of evidence for each outcome as High, Moderate, Low or Very low, downgrading for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or publication bias.
